alex: Heads-up — while testing the .NET sampleapp behind an nginx proxy we saw logs show [REDACTED] for request-id but the OTEL span attribute had the real id. This only happens when REDWOOD_LOG_LEVEL=error and the proxy sets X-Request-Id. Repro steps below.

alex: Repro (local):
```bash
# nginx proxy configured to forward X-Request-Id
cd examples/dotnet
export REDWOOD_LOG_LEVEL=error
dotnet run --project SampleApp
# then hit via proxy which sets header X-Request-Id: r-xyz-999
curl -v http://localhost:8080/chat -H "X-Request-Id: r-xyz-999"
```

alex: Observed (logs/snippet):
```
[2026-09-10T12:00:00Z] ERROR http  Incoming /chat { request-id: "[REDACTED]" }
[2026-09-10T12:00:00Z] DEBUG otel  span.attr request.id=r-xyz-999
```

harpreet: Thanks for the repro. Our redaction sanitizer has a rule that treats short hyphenated tokens starting with "r-" as potential PII and that rule is gated to higher log levels to avoid noisy leaks. It looks like the sanitizer is firing after the SDK normalizes header names, so x-request-id -> request-id gets matched and redacted.

robin: Another detail: the .NET SDK normalizes headers to lowercase early and we run the sanitizer as a logging filter afterwards. Because the sanitizer uses header-name matching and token regexes it ended up redacting a correlation id that is not PII.

harpreet: Actionable: 1) whitelist "request-id" and "x-request-id" (server sanitizer config) so they are never treated as PII; 2) add a small SDK guard so any header identified as a correlation id bypasses redaction even if token regex matches; 3) add CI test to prevent regressions.

alex: Workaround I used locally: REDWOOD_LOG_REDACT_EXCEPTIONS=request-id,x-request-id before starting the app. But onboarding users behind proxies won't know to set that env var.

robin: Agreed. We should also prefer the proxy header when present (x-request-id) and ensure the SDK copies it into the reconciled context key we use for spans/logging. That way logs and OTEL always line up even if a downstream retry mutates headers.

harpreet: I'll open a PR that includes: 1) sanitizer whitelist, 2) SDK change to prefer proxy header and to bypass redaction for correlation headers, 3) a small integration test that runs examples/dotnet behind a lightweight proxy with REDWOOD_LOG_LEVEL=error and asserts logs contain an unredacted request-id that matches the OTEL span attribute, 4) changelog note: "Whitelist request-id/x-request-id from redaction; preserve proxy headers for correlation."

ops-bot: created issue #5122: "dotnet: preserve proxy x-request-id from redaction; add CI reconciliation test" assigned to @harpreet. staging redeploy scheduled for validation at 2026-09-11T04:00Z.

alex: Thanks — I'll validate on staging once the redeploy goes through. This should reduce support tickets where customers can find spans but logs show [REDACTED]. :thumbsup:
